subject: Geography
description: Coal, iron ore, petroleum, bauxite — top producer states

questions.stem: India's largest producer of COAL is:

options.option_text: Odisha
Jharkhand
Chhattisgarh
West Bengal

questions.explanation: Jharkhand has been India's leading coal-producer for decades (Jharia, Bokaro, Karanpura coalfields). In very recent years, Chhattisgarh and Odisha have overtaken in some annual tallies — a mild staleness watchpoint. Historically + often in exam keys: Jharkhand.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The LARGEST iron-ore-producing state in India is:

options.option_text: Jharkhand
Odisha
Chhattisgarh
Karnataka

questions.explanation: Odisha — accounts for ~55% of India's iron-ore output (Keonjhar, Sundargarh). Chhattisgarh (Bailadila) second. Karnataka (Bellary-Hospet) third. Major iron-ore types: hematite (most common in India) and magnetite.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Match the MINERAL with its STATE-HUB. A. Bauxite (aluminium ore).  B. Mica.  C. Manganese.  D. Gold. List-II: 1. Odisha (Panchpatmali, Koraput).  2. Jharkhand / AP.  3. Madhya Pradesh (Balaghat).  4. Karnataka (Kolar / Hutti).
questions.explanation: Bauxite — Odisha leads; Jharkhand, Maharashtra follow. Mica — India was historically the world's top exporter; Jharkhand and Andhra Pradesh are key sources. Manganese — MP (Balaghat belt), Maharashtra. Gold — Kolar Gold Fields (Karnataka, now closed) / Hutti (still active). Mudgal (Andhra) for diamonds; Golconda earlier.

questions.stem: India's first OIL REFINERY was established at:

options.option_text: Mumbai High
Digboi (Assam)
Jamnagar
Barauni

questions.explanation: Digboi refinery — commissioned 1901 (Assam). Oldest continuously-operating refinery in Asia. Mumbai High (Bombay High) offshore field — discovered 1974, India's largest. Jamnagar (Reliance) — world's largest refinery complex today.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The LARGEST on-shore oilfield in India is:

options.option_text: Naharkatiya (Assam)
Ankleshwar (Gujarat)
Barmer (Rajasthan — Mangala field)
Digboi (Assam)

questions.explanation: Mangala oilfield (Barmer, Rajasthan) — discovered 2004, India's largest on-shore oilfield. Largest OFFSHORE is Mumbai High (ONGC). Ankleshwar and Naharkatiya are smaller but historically important fields.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: 'URANIUM CORPORATION OF INDIA' operates its mines primarily at:

options.option_text: Singhbhum (Jharkhand)
Bhilai (Chhattisgarh)
Bellary (Karnataka)
Panchpatmali (Odisha)

questions.explanation: UCIL (est. 1967, PSU under DAE) — Jaduguda mines in Singhbhum district of Jharkhand are India's main uranium source. Other deposits: Tummalapalle (Andhra Pradesh — 2007 discovery, one of the world's largest).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Match the MINING AREA with the state. A. Kolar.  B. Khetri.  C. Zawar.  D. Neyveli. List-II: 1. Karnataka (Gold).  2. Rajasthan (Copper).  3. Rajasthan (Zinc/lead).  4. Tamil Nadu (Lignite).
questions.explanation: Kolar Gold Fields (Karnataka) — gold. Khetri (Rajasthan) — copper (HCL). Zawar (Rajasthan) — lead-zinc (Hindustan Zinc). Neyveli (TN) — lignite mines + thermal power (Neyveli Lignite Corp).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Kudremukh iron ore mines, once among Asia's largest, are located in which district of Karnataka?

options.option_text: Ballari (Bellary) district, hub of iron ore belt in northern Karnataka
Chikmagalur district, situated in the Western Ghats of Karnataka
Hassan district, bordering the Western Ghats ranges of Karnataka
Chitradurga district, located in the Deccan plateau region of Karnataka

questions.explanation: Kudremukh iron ore deposits lie in Chikmagalur district within the Western Ghats. The Kudremukh Iron Ore Company Limited (KIOCL) operated there. Ballari is the common distractor because it hosts the Bellary-Hospet iron ore belt, but those are entirely separate deposits.

questions.stem: The Panna district of Madhya Pradesh holds India's only commercially active mines for which precious mineral?

options.option_text: Ruby, extracted from ancient metamorphic schists in Panna's hinterlands
Emerald, associated with the mica-schist belts of the Vindhyan ranges
Diamond, extracted from kimberlite pipes in the Vindhyan basin region
Sapphire, sourced from alluvial placer deposits along the Ken River

questions.explanation: Panna is India's sole commercially active diamond mining district. Diamonds occur here in ancient kimberlite pipes embedded in the Vindhyan sedimentary basin. Emerald is the top distractor because India does produce emeralds — but from Rajasthan's Rajnagar belt, not Panna.

questions.stem: India produces roughly 60% of the world's mica. Which of the following states is NOT among the three leading mica-producing states in India?

options.option_text: Jharkhand, which leads in sheet mica from the Koderma-Giridih belt
Andhra Pradesh, with major mica deposits concentrated in Nellore district
Rajasthan, producing mica from Bhilwara and Ajmer district areas
Odisha, despite being one of India's most mineral-rich eastern states

questions.explanation: The three dominant mica-producing states are Jharkhand (Koderma belt), Andhra Pradesh/Telangana (Nellore), and Rajasthan (Bhilwara, Ajmer). Odisha is mineral-rich in iron ore, chromite, and manganese but is NOT a significant mica producer — a classic confusion in exams.

questions.stem: The Sukinda valley, which holds over 95% of India's total reserves of a particular mineral ore, is located in which district of Odisha?

options.option_text: Bauxite ore, the primary aluminium-bearing mineral in peninsular India
Manganese ore, used extensively in steel and battery manufacturing
Chromite ore, essential for stainless steel and chrome plating industries
Magnetite ore, a high-grade iron ore variant used in direct smelting

questions.explanation: Sukinda valley in Jajpur district, Odisha, contains one of the world's largest chromite deposits and accounts for over 95% of India's chromite reserves. Manganese is a frequent distractor because Odisha also mines manganese, but Sukinda's global significance is specifically for chromite.

questions.stem: The Geological Survey of India (GSI), one of the world's oldest geological surveys, was established in 1851 primarily to fulfil which immediate colonial requirement?

options.option_text: 1851, to locate coal deposits for the expanding Indian railway network
1857, to survey mineral wealth after the First War of Independence
1872, to map strategic mineral belts for British industrial expansion
1906, to assess petroleum potential in the Assam-Arakan sedimentary basin

questions.explanation: GSI was founded in 1851 specifically to locate coal fields to fuel steam locomotives on the newly laid Indian railways. The 1857 option is a tempting distractor because of the historical significance of that year, but the GSI predates the revolt by six years.

questions.stem: The monazite-rich coastal placer sands of Kerala, which contain both thorium and rare-earth elements, are commercially processed by which central public sector undertaking at its Chavara facility?

options.option_text: Indian Rare Earths Ltd. (IREL), operating from Chavara in Kollam district
BARC extraction unit stationed at Kalpakkam in Tamil Nadu's coastal belt
Atomic Minerals Directorate (AMD) processing plant at Visakhapatnam, AP
NALCO rare-earth processing division located at Angul, Odisha's hub

questions.explanation: Indian Rare Earths Limited (IREL), a Government of India enterprise under DAE, processes monazite sands at its Chavara plant in Kollam district. BARC (Kalpakkam) is a reactor facility, not a mineral processing unit — the most common confusion. AMD surveys minerals but does not commercially process them.

questions.stem: The Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) mines Gondwana coal in the Pranahita-Godavari valley. After the 2014 state bifurcation, the state partner holding 51% equity stake is which of the following?

options.option_text: Andhra Pradesh, since SCCL's registered office historically remained in Hyderabad
Telangana, as all SCCL operational coalfields fell within its territory post-2014
Chhattisgarh, since the Gondwana coal basin extends into its eastern plateau
Maharashtra, whose Vidarbha coalfields share the same Gondwana formation belt

questions.explanation: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh in June 2014, every SCCL mine (Kothagudem, Ramagundam, Manuguru belts) fell within the newly formed Telangana. Telangana therefore inherited the 51% state stake. The Andhra Pradesh option is the most dangerous distractor because Hyderabad (where SCCL is headquartered) is now in Telangana, not AP.
